campaign.title: Agent Memory Bench
campaign.principle: Compare every memory boundary under an explicit dataset, context budget, reader, judge and repetition count.
constraints: Local models through Ollama where possible
Subscription readers isolated from private files and tools
Raw dataset and provider outputs remain local pending license and privacy review
campaign.headline: No system wins everywhere. Ingestion loss, temporal filtering, retrieval granularity and reader behavior can each reverse the ranking.

workflow.label: Sources
workflow.description: Immutable documents, conversations, events and task trajectories.

workflow.label: Ingestion
workflow.description: Raw storage, LLM extraction, deduplication, temporal metadata and Context Shards.

workflow.label: Representation
workflow.description: Chunks, atomic facts, graphs, event logs, snapshots and temporal indexes.

workflow.label: Retrieval
workflow.description: Long context, BM25, MiniLM, hybrid fusion, routing and graph expansion.

workflow.label: Context
workflow.description: Evidence recall, precision, temporal correctness, provenance and token budget.

workflow.label: Reader or agent
workflow.description: Local Qwen readers, isolated Codex readers and tool-using agents.

workflow.label: Verification
workflow.description: Exact and token metrics, paired tests, bootstrap, crash recovery and evidence audit.

runs.task: Memory, swarm, session, reload and persistence tests
runs.method: Compiled Rust test binaries and full offline workspace suite
runs.sample: 119 targeted tests plus the full workspace suite
runs.conclusion: The memory and swarm components have substantial local implementation evidence, but the repository as a whole is not green.
runs.limitation: Implementation tests do not establish end-to-end LLM quality.

runs.task: Evidence retrieval with temporal updates, rare exceptions, multi-hop and abstention
runs.method: Eight aligned retrieval strategies
runs.conclusion: Similarity maximizes broad recall, while explicit temporal filtering is required for current-state correctness.
runs.limitation: The corpus is small and synthetic; temporal correction is evaluated on five cases, and context budgets differ across methods.

runs.task: Answer generation after aligned retrieval
runs.method: Long context, hybrid, routed and parallel-fusion contexts
runs.conclusion: The stronger local reader used the full context best, despite substantially more noise and tokens.
runs.limitation: This result reverses on larger and more distractor-heavy public data.

runs.task: Compare orchestration topologies under one reader
runs.method: Single agent, pipeline, router, verification, retry and supervisor
runs.conclusion: The more complex topologies did not improve quality and verification rejected correct answers too often.
runs.limitation: Eight questions and one small reader do not characterize all multi-agent workloads.

runs.task: Atomic-fact extraction and temporal-window fidelity
runs.method: Two local extractors
runs.conclusion: The larger model mainly improved temporal metadata, not text F1.
runs.limitation: Text F1 penalizes useful paraphrases and does not fully measure semantic fidelity.

runs.task: Separate repeated observation, human decision and active prompt injection
runs.method: Three promotion policies
runs.sample: Two repeated patterns and one deferred candidate
runs.conclusion: Frequency must not equal approval; a separate decision registry preserves both active rules and rejected history.
runs.limitation: Human review decisions and review dates are synthetic.

runs.task: Current and historical state, provenance, abstention, expiry and retraction
runs.method: Snapshot, event-log scan and two temporal-index policies
runs.conclusion: The reviewed temporal index matches event-log correctness with less query-time work on this preregistered stream.
runs.limitation: The policies were designed for this deterministic workload and do not measure model extraction.

runs.task: Recover an append-only SQLite event log across process crashes
runs.method: WAL, synchronous FULL, crash immediately before and after commit
runs.sample: Six crash boundaries and twelve forced process exits
runs.conclusion: Uncommitted writes roll back, committed writes survive and the same semantic state is rebuilt in a second process.
runs.limitation: This does not cover arbitrary kernel failure, WAL-checkpoint failure, secure erasure or distributed durability.

runs.task: Separate jcode import consolidation from its hybrid retriever
runs.method: Official CLI import versus stable-ID upsert

series.diagnostic: Same retriever with stable source IDs

runs.conclusion: Most of the observed loss comes from aggressive consolidation during import, not from the hybrid retriever itself.
runs.limitation: The fixed top-5 path always returns candidates and cannot abstain.

runs.task: Separate raw storage from LLM memory extraction
runs.method: Mem0 OSS with Qdrant and nomic-embed-text

series.diagnostic: Raw dense storage preserved every source

runs.conclusion: In this configuration, extraction adds cost, duplication and false provenance without improving retrieval.
runs.limitation: The result is specific to a small local extractor, atomic source documents and dense retrieval without the optional BM25 extra.

runs.task: Retrieve annotated dialogue-turn evidence
runs.method: BM25, MiniLM and 50/50 hybrid
runs.conclusion: Turn-level evidence retrieval is difficult, especially for multi-hop questions.
runs.limitation: This run evaluates retrieval, not final answers.

runs.task: Measure retrieval-unit granularity under equal item and equal word budgets
runs.method: Turns, overlapping windows and full sessions
runs.conclusion: Five sessions look best only because they inject almost 22 times more words; local windows win under a common budget.
runs.limitation: The best window size depends on the retriever and MiniLM truncation.

runs.task: Retrieve annotated evidence sessions
runs.method: BM25, MiniLM and hybrid
runs.conclusion: Session retrieval is much easier than LoCoMo turn retrieval under the same top-k.
runs.limitation: The units and context sizes differ, so the raw percentage is not a product leaderboard.

runs.task: Paired answerable and near-miss challenge
runs.method: No context, BM25 and hybrid with two isolated Codex readers
runs.sample: Eight paired questions, 16 prompts per condition
runs.conclusion: BM25 and hybrid were statistically indistinguishable on this diagnostic slice; multi-session reading remained the main failure.
runs.limitation: This is not the official LLM-judged LongMemEval score and eight pairs are too few to rank readers.

runs.task: Answer from a static 456-fact memory with contradictory updates
runs.method: Full context, BM25 top-20 and hybrid top-20
runs.conclusion: Compressed retrieval significantly beats full context on both 6k tasks, but multi-hop remains very weak.
runs.limitation: The official substring metric can reward answers that contain both the correct and a contradictory value.

runs.task: Retrieval and coverage across classification, recommendation, QA, event ordering and summarization
runs.method: Deterministic BM25 and lexical ablations
runs.sample: 500 ICL questions, 200 ReDial, 200 RULER, 1,500 EventQA, 71 DetectiveQA and 100 books

highlights.name: Book keypoint lexical recall, BM25 budget
Book keypoint lexical recall, full context

runs.conclusion: Memory presence and retrieval ability are separate limits; distractors and query construction cause large losses even when the target exists.
runs.limitation: These are layer-specific ablations, not the official end-to-end scores.

runs.task: Retrieve required multi-hop facts
runs.method: Official IRBM25Memory and paired MiniLM sample
runs.conclusion: BM25 is strong on the official lexical proxy and beats MiniLM at top-2 on the paired sample.
runs.limitation: The proxy saturates at generous context and does not evaluate final multi-hop answers.

runs.task: Reproduce the released safety classifier
runs.method: Official CLI on CPU without NF4
runs.conclusion: Aggregate AUROC is close to the released artifact, while per-event probabilities reproduce poorly.
runs.limitation: Hardware and quantization differ from the eight-GPU released run.

runs.task: Compare graph ingestion, source retrieval and temporal correctness
runs.method: Cognee and Graphiti with the same Qwen 2.5 14B extractor
runs.conclusion: Cognee covers more sources but is slower and unstable; Graphiti reads quickly but loses more information and repeats an ingestion timeout.
runs.limitation: Eight synthetic documents are not a general graph-memory benchmark.

runs.task: Retrieve official evidence sentences from fixed chunks
runs.method: BM25, MiniLM, hybrid and deterministic chunk-neighborhood expansion
runs.sample: 20 novels, 2,010 questions, 7,003 chunks and 4,689 evidence sentences
runs.conclusion: Replacing two top-five chunks with graph neighbors significantly reduced evidence recall under this operator.
runs.limitation: This is not a real entity-relation GraphRAG engine and the lexical judge covers only 20.9 percent of evidence.

runs.task: Run the official LightRAG path end to end
runs.method: LightRAG 1.2.5, Qwen 2.5 14B and nomic-embed-text
runs.sample: One 29,099-word novel and one requested question
runs.conclusion: The official local path remained in document processing beyond the declared budget and exposed no final index or answer.
runs.limitation: An operational timeout is not evidence that LightRAG fails in general.

runs.task: Validate MemoryData runner presets and one end-to-end question
runs.method: Long context, BM25 top-10 and top-2, dense top-2
runs.conclusion: The runner and three preset families execute, but query construction dominates relevance on the tested question.
runs.limitation: One all-zero question cannot rank MemoryData methods; the repository license was not verified at its root.

runs.task: Persist and retrieve agent memory through MemFS
runs.method: Official smoke and complete headless scenario
runs.conclusion: Letta Code can write, version and recover a memory file in a clean local agent state.
runs.limitation: Its agent-driven file exploration is not directly comparable to passive top-k retrieval.

runs.task: Answer or abstain on matched answerable and near-miss pairs
runs.method: Hybrid retrieval over turn chunks versus user-turn chunks
runs.conclusion: User-turn chunking improved deterministic overall accuracy by 8.6 points, but the paired decision difference was not statistically distinguishable on 29 pairs.
runs.limitation: Answer matching outside the original alias set is a strict lower bound, and this run has no no-context memorization control. Tool avoidance was prompt-enforced; no tool traces were found in retained stderr, but command-level disabling was added only afterward.

runs.task: Retrieve answer evidence as contradictory memory grows
runs.method: BM25 top-20 and iterative lexical expansion
runs.conclusion: Single-hop evidence stayed nearly saturated at every scale, while multi-hop BM25 hit@20 fell from 41% at 6k to 13% at 262k; iterative expansion recovered some evidence at much higher latency.
runs.limitation: This isolates answer-string evidence coverage before generation and is not the official end-to-end benchmark score.

runs.task: Read contradictory memory from 32k through 262k scale
runs.method: Full context, BM25 top-20 and hybrid top-20
runs.sample: 15 fixed questions across six multi-hop and single-hop variants
runs.conclusion: Single-hop retrieval remained useful as memory grew, while multi-hop reading stayed weak; raw 262k contexts exceeded the Codex input-character ceiling but compressed retrieval paths ran.
runs.limitation: Only 15 fixed questions per variant were evaluated, and the official substring metric can reward overbroad contradictory answers. Tool avoidance was prompt-enforced; no tool traces were found in retained stderr, but command-level disabling was added only afterward.

runs.task: Answer multi-hop deep-research questions from bounded memory
runs.method: Visible documents versus BM25 chunk retrieval at top-1, top-2 and top-5
runs.sample: 10 fixed questions in each of the 3-hop, 4-hop and 5-6-hop strata
runs.conclusion: The provisional semantic judge favored bm25_k2 with a macro score of 0.743.
runs.limitation: The semantic score is not human-calibrated. It remains provisional until two blinded annotators complete the fixed calibration pack; exact and substring match are overly strict for these long-form answers.

runs.task: Retrieve evidence for complex reasoning and fact questions
runs.method: Cognee default concurrency, Kuzu and LanceDB embedded, top-5
runs.conclusion: Cognee did not finish ingestion inside the shared 30-minute ceiling, so retrieval quality was not scored.
runs.limitation: This is one local model, one 20-document slice and one repetition. A timeout is an operational-capacity result, not evidence that the engine can never achieve good retrieval quality.

runs.task: Retrieve evidence for complex reasoning and fact questions
runs.method: Cognee single-item local-provider ablation, Kuzu and LanceDB embedded, top-5
runs.conclusion: Cognee did not finish ingestion inside the shared 30-minute ceiling, so retrieval quality was not scored.
runs.limitation: This is one local model, one 20-document slice and one repetition. A timeout is an operational-capacity result, not evidence that the engine can never achieve good retrieval quality.

runs.task: Retrieve evidence for complex reasoning and fact questions
runs.method: Graphiti single-coroutine ingestion, FalkorDB Lite, top-5
runs.conclusion: Graphiti built 13 of 20 documents inside the shared ingestion budget; retrieval metrics therefore describe a partial index.
runs.limitation: This is one local model, one 20-document slice and one repetition. A timeout is an operational-capacity result, not evidence that the engine can never achieve good retrieval quality.

runs.task: Extract and replay corrections, expirations, retractions and duplicates
runs.method: Qwen 2.5 14B extraction followed by deterministic event replay
runs.conclusion: The selected final answer was always correct, but complete active state exactness was only 85%; the broader state metric exposed stale records hidden by answer-only scoring.
runs.limitation: This controlled corpus is synthetic and bounded. The observable-field score is explicitly posthoc; strict field accuracy remains the primary extraction metric.

runs.task: Recover temporal, full-text, vector and graph views after injected crashes
runs.method: Crash injection around one transactional generation manifest
runs.conclusion: All eight injected boundaries recovered the same semantic state and source IDs as the uninterrupted build, with no orphan generation.
runs.limitation: This validates one local SQLite-backed design. It does not prove distributed durability, arbitrary kernel failure behavior or hardware flush guarantees.

runs.task: Remove retracted, expired and tombstoned data from every active surface
runs.method: Logical deletion, index rebuild, SQLite VACUUM and backup verification
runs.sample: Seven active storage and retrieval surfaces
runs.conclusion: All seven active surfaces and the new backup were clean after compaction while hashed audit events remained verifiable.
runs.limitation: The old backup intentionally retains deleted payloads and needs its own retention policy. SQLite VACUUM does not prove physical SSD flash erasure.

systems.name: jcode
systems.tested: Rust implementation, memory import and retrieval, session resume and swarm
systems.headline: Strong local machinery; aggressive consolidation loses distinct updates and exceptions.

systems.name: Mem0 OSS
systems.tested: Raw and inferred ingestion with embedded Qdrant
systems.headline: Raw storage preserved the small corpus; local extraction added latency, duplication and false provenance.

systems.name: Cognee
systems.tested: Local semantic graph and temporal retrieval
systems.headline: Higher average coverage than Graphiti, with large run variance and slow retrieval.

systems.name: Graphiti
systems.tested: Local temporal graph with FalkorDB Lite
systems.headline: Fast and stable reading, but incomplete ingestion and historical reconstruction.

systems.name: Letta Code
systems.tested: Official headless scenario and MemFS persistence
systems.headline: Functional file memory that needs an agentic, not passive-retrieval, comparison.

systems.name: MemGym
systems.tested: Tests, τ²-bench tasks, MemGym-DR retrieval and MemRM
systems.headline: Useful harness for separating memory and environment, with proxy and hardware caveats.

systems.name: MemoryData
systems.tested: Official data loading and three preset families on one EventQA question
systems.headline: Runner works, but the current query and single sample cannot rank methods.

systems.name: AGORA
systems.headline: No public dataset and official local runner were located for this campaign.

systems.name: Zep managed
systems.tested: Managed service excluded; Graphiti tested separately
systems.headline: Requires a service account and must not be conflated with the open Graphiti engine.

findings: No architecture wins independently of dataset, retrieval unit, context budget and reader.
A top-k comparison is invalid when units differ materially in size.
Explicit temporal filtering solves failures that similarity alone does not guarantee.
Ingestion and consolidation can destroy more information than retrieval loses.
LLM extraction can preserve useful text while falsifying provenance.
More agents, verifiers or loops can reduce quality and multiply cost.
A full context can beat RAG on a tiny corpus and lose badly on a distractor-heavy one.
A strong retrieval score does not guarantee that the reader resolves multi-hop contradictions.
Temperature zero does not make structured LLM ingestion deterministic.
Aggregate reproduction can hide poor agreement on individual events.
Chunk boundaries can change final reading quality even when evidence-session recall is unchanged.
Multi-hop evidence retrieval degrades with memory scale even when single-hop retrieval remains saturated.
At 262k scale, compressed retrieval remained executable while raw full contexts exceeded the reader input ceiling.
On the fixed MemGym-DR slice, BM25 top-2 improved the provisional paired semantic-judge score by 0.108 over visible documents alone; top-5 was not consistently better.
Under the aligned 30-minute local GraphRAG budget, Graphiti indexed 13 of 20 documents while Cognee completed neither its default nor serial ingestion path.
Answer-only temporal scoring hid stale active records: selected values were 100% correct while complete active-state exactness was 85%.
A deterministic four-view derived index recovered the uninterrupted semantic state at all eight injected crash boundaries.
Deletion and compaction removed payloads from all seven active surfaces, but old backups still require an explicit retention policy.
limitations: The synthetic common corpus is small and intentionally adversarial.
Several public-dataset experiments evaluate retrieval or lexical coverage, not final answers.
Model-backed comparisons use a mixture of local Ollama readers and isolated subscription readers.
Not every campaign is repeated; the registry records repetition counts explicitly.
Raw official-dataset contexts and provider outputs are not published pending license and privacy review.
AGORA and the managed Zep product were not reproduced locally.
The GraphRAG-Bench neighbor ablation is not a complete GraphRAG engine.
There is no aggregate leaderboard because the current protocols are not all commensurable.
MemGym semantic scores remain provisional until two blinded humans complete the fixed 40-item calibration pack.
The aligned GraphRAG comparison is one 20-document slice, one local model and one repetition; ingestion failures are capacity observations, not universal engine rankings.
Priority 3 temporal, crash and deletion results use controlled local fixtures and do not establish distributed-system guarantees.
SQLite VACUUM verifies the rebuilt database file but does not prove physical SSD flash erasure; old backups retain data until separately expired.
